acceptedAnswer.text: Inflation is the rate at which the general price level of goods and services rises, reducing the purchasing power of money over time.

mainEntity.name: How does inflation affect purchasing power?

acceptedAnswer.text: As inflation increases, the same amount of money buys fewer goods and services, reducing its real value.
Future cost is calculated using compound inflation: Present Cost × (1 + inflation rate)^years.
Moderate inflation is normal in growing economies, but high inflation erodes savings and purchasing power.
